title: Beating the Bad-Cavity Limit via Auxiliary-Emitter Linewidth Squeezing
authors: Youke Xu, Zeyang Liao, Xue-hua Wang
abstract: Strong coupling in cavity QED is conventionally achieved at the expense of either high cavity quality factors or ultrasmall mode volumes, a trade-off that fundamentally constrains practical implementations. Here, we circumvent this limitation by introducing two nonidentical auxiliary emitters with opposite detunings into a bad cavity. This hybrid system supports a subradiant mode that significantly squeeze the effective cavity linewidth, creating an ultra-narrow transmission window at the cavity frequency. As a result, a target emitter placed in this engineered environment exhibits prolonged vacuum Rabi oscillations and resolved spontaneous emission splitting, which are clear signatures of strong coupling, even though the bare cavity remains in the weak-coupling regime. Our scheme thus transforms a bad cavity into an effective platform for strong-coupling physics, with potential applications in quantum computation and quantum sensing.
summary: The authors propose a method to enable strong coupling physics in optical cavities that are otherwise too lossy or weakly coupled (bad cavities). They achieve this by incorporating two specially detuned auxiliary emitters, which engineer an effective subradiant mode that narrows the cavity linewidth. This allows for clear spectroscopic signatures of strong coupling, opening up practical avenues for quantum computation and sensing.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is overcoming the fundamental trade-off in cavity QED where achieving strong coupling requires either high quality factors or ultrasmall mode volumes.
main_result: By introducing two nonidentical auxiliary emitters with opposite detunings into a bad cavity, the system can engineer an ultra-narrow transmission window and achieve signatures of strong coupling (like Rabi oscillations) even when the bare cavity is in the weak-coupling regime.
method: The analysis uses quantum Langevin equations and eigenvalue analysis on the effective Hamiltonian to derive the transmission spectrum and characterize the resulting subradiant modes.
model_or_system: The system models a hybrid setup: a bad optical cavity coupled to two nonidentical auxiliary emitters and one target emitter. The dynamics are governed by the total Hamiltonian, analyzed via master equations or Langevin equations.
key_observables: Effective cavity linewidth ($\kappa_{eff}$), transmission spectrum ($|T_{CA}|^2$), prolonged vacuum Rabi oscillations in the target emitter's population, and spontaneous emission spectral splitting.
important_parameters: Auxiliary detunings ($\delta_1 = -\delta_2 = \delta$), coupling strengths ($G$, $g$), cavity decay rate ($\kappa$), and emitter decay rates ($\gamma$).
main_assumptions: Key approximations include assuming $\gamma \ll \kappa$ and analyzing the central peak using specific functional forms derived from the full system Hamiltonian.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate schematic linewidth reduction, transmission spectra comparing different emitter configurations (bare vs. non-identical), and time evolution plots showing Rabi oscillations in target excitation probability ($P_T(t)$).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from identifying the physical limitation to developing a theoretical model using Langevin equations, deriving analytical approximations for linewidth reduction via destructive interference, and finally demonstrating strong coupling signatures through numerical simulation of population dynamics.
why_interesting: This work provides an elegant engineering solution to a major practical bottleneck in cavity QED—the bad-cavity limit—by manipulating the system's spectral response using auxiliary components. This has direct implications for building quantum devices.
